overall: The Board violated the Open Meeting Law by giving executive session topics too little detail in both the notice and the chair's pre-session statement. It did not violate the law by taking up a topic added the day before, and the AG found no notice-posting violation for tenants.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board discussed a topic not listed on the meeting notice, a project contract added to the agenda the day of the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by discussing the topic during its February 12 meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the executive session topics were not described with enough detail in the meeting notice and in the chair's verbal statement before executive session.
allegations.key_passage: the Board did not include enough detail about the topic either in the notice or in the announcement prior to the executive session.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board improperly convened in executive session at the February 12 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: we find the discussion about the Open Meeting Law complaint was properly held

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the notice, though posted with the Town Clerk, was not posted for tenants in the Housing Authority building.
allegations.key_passage: The Town's official notice posting method is the bulletin board outside of Town Hall, thus it is not required to post notice in the Housing Authority building.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law (ordered).
Board may not rely on the Open Meeting Law to withhold its February 12, 2015 executive session minutes, since the session did not fully comply.
The portion of the executive session minutes discussing whether the Board could honor the grievance request in open session should be released in its entirety (footnote 6).
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
